Level 2 · Intermediate · Week 1

Welcome Back, Python

Every value has a type, and f-strings glue values into friendly messages.

What you will learn

  • The four basic types of value: whole numbers, decimal numbers, text and True/False.
  • How to build messages with f-strings.
  • How to turn typed answers into numbers with int().
  • How to make smarter choices with and, or and not.

The big idea: every value has a type

Python sorts every value into a type. The type decides what Python can do with it. Here are the four types you will use most:

Quotes are the big clue. 7 is a number, but "7" is text that happens to show a 7. You can ask Python for the type of anything. Type this in the Thonny Shell (after >>>):

Try it in the Shell

type(7)        # <class 'int'>
type("7")      # <class 'str'>
type(3.5)      # <class 'float'>
type(True)     # <class 'bool'>

Bug hunt: text plus a number

Try "5" + 5 in the Shell. Python shows a red error message. Always read it from the bottom line up:

TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str

“Concatenate” means “glue together”. Python can glue text to text, but not text to a number. This matters because input() always gives back text, even when you type a number. Turn it into a whole number with int():

level = int(input("Level? "))     # the player types 4
print(level + 1)                  # 5

f-strings: fill in the blanks

Put an f in front of the quotes, and Python fills every pair of curly brackets with a value. It works with any type, so you never have to worry about text plus a number.

Smarter choices: and, or, not

Word True when… Game example
and both sides are true has_key and level >= 3
or at least one side is true level >= 10 or has_map
not the opposite not game_over

Each side needs a full comparison: write energy >= 5 or energy == 1, not energy >= 5 or 1.

TipHero names, not real names

Your real name, school, address and birthday are personal information. Keep them private. In our programs you always type a made-up hero name or nickname.

Exercise1.2: Mood Meter

Folder: exercises/week01/ex-mood-meter. The program asks for your energy (0–10) and whether you had a snack, then draws a meter. Finish mood_for():

  • “Super charged”: energy 8 or more and a snack.

  • “Ready to play”: energy 5 or more or a snack.

  • “Recharge time”: everything else.

Before you run it, predict the mood. Then run and check.

energy snack? my guess the program said

3 no

New words

type
The kind of value: int, float, str or bool. It decides what Python can do with it.
int
A whole number, like 7 or -2.
float
A number with a decimal point, like 3.5 or 2.0.
str (string)
Text inside quotes, like "cat" or "7" .
bool
True or False. Comparisons like level >= 3 give a bool.
f-string
Text with an f in front. Curly brackets inside are filled with values.
TypeError
An error that means “these two types do not go together”.
personal information
Facts that say who you really are or where to find you. Keep it private.

  • you have the golden key and you are level 3 or more, or

  • you are level 10 or more (legends do not need keys).

  3. Run it three times and check what happened:

    key yes, level 2: opens ☐ shut ☐
    key no, level 12: opens ☐ shut ☐

ChallengePredict, then check

Write what each line prints. Then type it into the Thonny Shell to check.

print(3 > 2 and 5 > 9)
print(3 > 2 or 5 > 9)
print(not 3 > 2)
print("7" + "7")
print(int("7") + 7)
